examples.solution_text:
The coefficient of $x$ is $3$. Integrate cosine to sine and divide by $3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 9\cos(3x+4)\,dx\\&=\frac{9}{3}\sin(3x+4)+C\\&=3\sin(3x+4)+C\end{aligned}$

The coefficient of $x$ is $-4$. Keep the minus sign from integrating sine, then divide by $-4$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 8\sin(6-4x)\,dx\\&=-\frac{8}{-4}\cos(6-4x)+C\\&=2\cos(6-4x)+C\end{aligned}$

The coefficient of $x$ is $\frac{1}{6}$, so dividing by it multiplies by $6$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 2\sec^{2}\left(\frac{x}{6}+1\right)\,dx\\&=2\times6\tan\left(\frac{x}{6}+1\right)+C\\&=12\tan\left(\frac{x}{6}+1\right)+C\end{aligned}$

Integrate each term separately, dividing by its own inner coefficient.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\left(10\cos 5x-3\sin\frac{x}{2}+12\sec^{2}4x\right)\,dx\\&=\frac{10}{5}\sin 5x-3\left(-2\cos\frac{x}{2}\right)+\frac{12}{4}\tan4x+C\\&=2\sin5x+6\cos\frac{x}{2}+3\tan4x+C\end{aligned}$

Divide by $2$, then substitute the limits into the whole angle in radians.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{0}^{\pi/12}\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac12\sin\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]_{0}^{\pi/12}\\&=\frac12\left(\sin\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\\&=\frac12\left(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{2-\sqrt3}{4}\end{aligned}$

The angle ranges from $\pi$ to $\frac{5\pi}{4}$, so the interval contains no asymptote of secant squared.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{0}^{\pi/12}\sec^{2}(3x+\pi)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac13\tan(3x+\pi)\right]_{0}^{\pi/12}\\&=\frac13\left(\tan\frac{5\pi}{4}-\tan\pi\right)\\&=\frac13(1-0)\\&=\frac13\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A function has $f'(x)=4\cos2x$ and $f(0)=3$. Find $f(x)$ and $f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$.
Find $\int\frac{2}{p}\sec^{2}(px+r)\,dx$, where $p$ and $r$ are real constants and $p\ne0$.
examples.solution_text:
The inner coefficient is $p$. Divide by $p$ as well as retaining the factor $\frac{2}{p}$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\frac{2}{p}\sec^{2}(px+r)\,dx\\&=\frac{2}{p}\times\frac{1}{p}\tan(px+r)+C\\&=\frac{2}{p^{2}}\tan(px+r)+C\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored eight examples covering all five assessed methods, with separate editable prompts and solutions. Checked new working by differentiation and endpoint substitution. Continuation gutters are explicit where needed; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. These symbolic integration tasks need no diagrams. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged; no files were written. Independent review and actual visual capture remain later stages.

examples.derivation: Integrating gives (9/3)sin(3x+4)+C = 3sin(3x+4)+C. Differentiation returns 9cos(3x+4). Matches the constant-multiple cosine type at source line 1521.
The inner derivative is -4, giving -8/(-4)cos(6-4x)+C = 2cos(6-4x)+C. Differentiation returns 8sin(6-4x). Matches Development Q5f with a constant multiplier.
Dividing the multiplier 2 by 1/6 gives 12tan(x/6+1)+C. Its derivative is 12(1/6)sec²(x/6+1), the given integrand. Source Foundation Q1l/Q1q and line 1508 support this form.
Termwise primitives are 2sin(5x), 6cos(x/2), and 3tan(4x). Their derivatives are respectively 10cos(5x), -3sin(x/2), and 12sec²(4x). The result matches the source Development Q6b method.
The primitive is (1/2)sin(2x+π/3). The endpoint angles are π/3 and π/2, giving (1/2)(1-√3/2) = (2-√3)/4. Source cosine Example and Guided Practice d support the method.

The angle interval [π,5π/4] contains no value π/2+nπ, including endpoints. Evaluating (1/3)tan(3x+π) gives (1/3)(1-0) = 1/3. This adapts the source secant-squared Example and follows its asymptote restriction.

Integration gives f(x)=2sin(2x)+C. Since f(0)=3, C=3. Thus f(π/6)=2sin(π/3)+3=√3+3. Differentiation and the initial condition both check. Source Development Q7b supports integration, determination of C, and subsequent evaluation.
For p≠0, retaining 2/p and dividing again by p gives (2/p²)tan(px+r)+C. Differentiation returns (2/p)sec²(px+r). This matches source Mastery Q9c with an adapted multiplier.
